subject: english-literature
title: Feminist Traditions
welcome_lead: Feminist criticism traces women's writing and asks how texts construct gender. From Wollstonecraft to Butler, the tradition is rich.
meta_desc: English Literature: feminist cultural contexts — Showalter, Cixous, Butler.
final_note: Reading as a feminist is not adding politics — it is naming the politics already there.

concepts.def: Movement and theory asserting the political, social and economic equality of women.
Showalter's study of women's writing as a distinct tradition.
Judith Butler's theory that gender is enacted rather than essential.
A social system in which men hold primary power.
Gothic fiction by women foregrounding women's confinement and anxiety.
Gilbert and Gubar's image of Victorian women writers' suppressed creative anger.

walkthroughs.body_html: Their reading of Bertha Mason as Jane's double opened a feminist tradition. The 'madwoman' figure is the silenced rage of women writers themselves.
For Butler, gender is the repeated stylisation of the body. Reading Orlando or Mrs Dalloway through performativity opens questions of how characters become 'feminine'.
Ann Radcliffe and the Brontes use gothic conventions — confinement, mysterious men, decaying houses — to encode women's experience of patriarchy.
